creator: Brian De Palma
notes: Carlito's old girlfriend Gail, a dancer, lives here; the film shot her building on Gay Street, and Carlito is arrested at the street's end at Waverly Place. No source places Carlito's own home.
source_quote: Gail's apartment is 17 Gay Street, also in the village

creator: Abel Ferrara
address_as_given: his suite at the top of the Plaza Hotel
notes: Out of Sing Sing, the drug lord lives and runs his operation from a suite high in the Plaza Hotel. The film shot in the real hotel, so the story building and the filmed building are the same.
source_quote: From his opulent retreat at the top of Manhattan’s Plaza Hotel, Frank coordinates a series of similar hits
source2_quote: gave him permission to film at the Plaza Hotel at no charge

creator: Luc Besson
notes: The hitman's apartment is down the hall from Mathilda's family. The 97th Street building was used for exteriors only; the stairwells and corridors were shot inside the Hotel Chelsea on West 23rd Street.
source_quote: Leon's Apartment, 71 East 97th Street and Park Avenue, Manhattan.
source2_quote: the stairwell and corridors are those of the famous, and unbelievably closed, Hotel Chelsea, 222 West 23rd Street

household: with her father, stepmother, half-sister and little brother
creator: Luc Besson
notes: Mathilda's family lives down the hall from Léon until corrupt DEA agents kill them. Same exterior as Léon's apartment; interiors were the Hotel Chelsea.
source_quote: Léon and Mathilda's apartment building on the northwest corner of E 97th St & Park Ave
source2_quote: The hotel of precocious Mathilda (Natalie Portman), where she loses her family in a savage attack, 71 97th Street at Park Avenue

household: with his parents Arkady and Irina; his estranged brother Joshua grew up here
creator: James Gray
notes: The Soviet Jewish immigrant family lives in Brighton Beach; Joshua, the hitman son, stays in a hotel when he comes back. No source names the building.
source_quote: reconnects with his estranged Soviet immigrant family in Brooklyn. The title is a reference to Brighton Beach, a Brooklyn community nicknamed
source2_quote: Joshua stands outside his family's apartment, where he is spotted by one of his old friends Sasha

creator: Michael Winner
notes: The architect's apartment, where muggers attack his wife and daughter. Movie-locations.com writes Riverside Avenue, which is a slip for Riverside Drive. The story itself gives no address beyond Manhattan.
source_quote: Paul Kersey's Apartment, 33 Riverside Drive and West 75th Street, Manhattan.
source2_quote: The apartment of architect Paul Kersey (Bronson) is 33 Riverside Avenue at West 75th Street on the West Side

creator: John Schlesinger
address_as_given: 435 West 47th Street, between Ninth and Tenth Avenues
notes: The Columbia graduate student's apartment, where his brother Doc dies after being stabbed. The film shot it in Hell's Kitchen; no source gives a story address.
source_quote: Thomas Babington's Apartment, 435 West 47th Street (btw 9th and 10th Avenue) Manhattan.

creator: Harold Becker
address_as_given: 45 West 89th Street, between Columbus Avenue and Central Park West
notes: The apartment of the suspect Frank Keller falls for, where the killer, her ex-husband, finally turns up. Many interiors were shot in Toronto.
source_quote: Helen Cruger Apartment, 45 West 89th Street and Central Park West, Manhattan.
source2_quote: Keller lives just to the north on 85th Street, and Cruger even further north at 45 West 89th Street

creator: Harold Becker
address_as_given: 85th Street, north of 365 West End Avenue
notes: The burned-out homicide detective's apartment was filmed on 85th Street on the West Side, but no source names the building, so the mark is placed near West End Avenue with a wide radius.
source_quote: Keller lives just to the north on 85th Street, and Cruger even further north at 45 West 89th Street

creator: Phil Joanou
notes: An undercover cop comes back to the neighborhood he grew up in, where his friend Jackie Flannery's family runs an Irish gang modeled on the Westies. No building is named for anyone's home.
source_quote: Terry Noonan (Sean Penn) returns home to New York's Hells Kitchen after a ten year absence.
source2_quote: Irish-American Terry Noonan returns to Hell's Kitchen in New York City after a long absence

creator: Stuart Rosenberg
address_as_given: an Italian neighborhood of Greenwich Village
notes: The two cousins live and scheme in the Italian South Village; the film shot shops on Sullivan Street near West Houston. No source places either man's apartment. The Vincent Patrick novel is not covered here.
source_quote: In an Italian neighborhood of Greenwich Village, cousins Charlie Moran

household: with his family; Max, Patsy, Cockeye and Dominic are neighborhood boys
work: Once Upon a Time in America
creator: Sergio Leone
address_as_given: a Jewish enclave in Manhattan's Lower East Side
notes: Noodles grows up poor on the Lower East Side and runs a gang there from 1918. The film's 1920s street scenes were shot in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, under the Williamsburg Bridge, not in Manhattan, and no building is identified as his home.
source_quote: born in either 1903 or 1904 into poverty in a Jewish enclave in Manhattan's Lower East Side
source2_quote: The twenties ‘Lower East Side’ neighbourhood, where Noodles and Max first meet up, was indeed filmed on the streets below the towering Williamsburg Bridge

creator: Billy Wilder
address_as_given: 231 East 55th Street (a rooftop set on Hahn's Warehouse)
notes: The opening pan ends at Don's window with a bottle hung outside. Researchers traced it to a set built on the roof of Hahn's Warehouse, 231 East 55th Street, around the corner from P.J. Clarke's; the warehouse is demolished. Another blog estimates 209 East 54th Street instead. The film gives no story address.
source_quote: The camera ends on Don Birnam’s apartment window at 231 E. 55th Street with a bottle hanging on a string outside it.
source2_quote: The movie was filmed on location in Don’s apartment, a fourth story walkup at what appears to be (according to my analysis) 209 East 54th Street.

creator: Norman Jewison
address_as_given: his apartment above the Cammareri Bros. bakery, Henry Street at Sackett Street
notes: Ronny, the one-handed baker, lives over the family bakery, the real Cammareri Bros. at 502 Henry Street, which closed in 1998. The bakery scenes were shot there; a neighborhood blogger believes the apartment interior was too, with its entrance on Sackett Street, but that is unconfirmed.
source_quote: In the movie, Ronny’s apartment is above the bakery.
source2_quote: The "Moonstruck" scene was filmed in the bakery's storefront and in the basement at 502 Henry Street.

creator: Abby Mann
notes: The show puts the lieutenant's apartment in Greenwich Village but shot its exterior on Fifth Avenue at 12th Street.
source_quote: The apartment was supposedly in the Village, but the exteriors were shot at 5th Ave and 12th St.

creator: Abby Mann
notes: Only the intersection is given for the exterior, not the building, so this is graded below screen_exterior.
source_quote: The apartment was supposedly in the Village, but the exteriors were shot at 5th Ave and 12th St.

creator: Jonathan Nolan
notes: Finch gives Reese the loft for his birthday in 2012. Baxter Street's numbers run nowhere near 810, so the number is invented; the mark sits on Baxter Street across from Columbus Park, as the show says.
source_quote: Located at 810 Baxter St., it faces Columbus Park, where Reese occasionally plays xiangqi

creator: Jonathan Nolan
notes: Finch's late partner moved into this loft with an indoor pool after his divorce; his son Will inherits it. The show gives no story address; the scenes were filmed in the real townhouse, a former Con Edison station. Setting years are estimated: Nathan dies in 2010.
source_quote: Located at 214 Lafayette St., the building is a five-story townhouse with an indoor pool
source2_quote: The loft is where Nathan Ingram moved after his divorce.
